clue.text: Robert's working with boy to produce Anglo-Indian phrasebook

parts.note: Hob is an old pet form of the name Robert, so Robert's gives Hob's
someone working is on the job, shortened here to on job
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A man called Robert teams up with a lad to put together a guide to Anglo-Indian speech.
explanation.walkthrough: HOB is an old pet form of Robert, now rarely heard. Hobson-Jobson is the famous 1886 glossary of Anglo-Indian words and phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobson-Jobson is the title of the classic Victorian glossary of words borrowed from India into English.

clue.text: Henry and I save swimmer in Atlantic

parts.note: Hal is the familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
save in the sense of except, like but in 'all but one'

explanation.surface: Henry and the speaker rescue someone swimming in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like a verb about rescue, but it means 'except', giving BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish found in the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Suit to keep in good condition

definitions.meaning: suit as a verb, be appropriate for

explanation.surface: A note on dressing smartly and staying healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to suit or be proper for; split in two, the word reads 'be fit', stay healthy and in shape.

clue.text: Possibly a newspaper is getting editor straightened out

parts.note: a newspaper is an example of an organ, a publication speaking for a group

explanation.surface: A newspaper takes on an editor and sorts out its affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something organised has been put in order, tidied and arranged.

clue.text: A name given to boys mother and devoted wife

indicators.note: given to says the following pieces are attached after the mother's name

parts.note: Jo March is the mother in Louisa May Alcott's novel Jo's Boys

explanation.surface: A name chosen for a family of boys by their mother, a loyal wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan are the proverbial devoted elderly married couple; Jo's Boys is Alcott's sequel to Little Women, in which Jo is the mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of the rhyme Darby and Joan stands for the faithful, loving old wife.

clue.text: Mark a left-winger, keenly pursued

parts.note: a badge is a distinguishing mark or emblem
a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left

explanation.surface: A socialist is given a distinguishing emblem and hounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left-winger' suggests a footballer, but it is a political red.
explanation.definitionFit: To be badgered is to be harassed and pestered persistently.

clue.text: Volunteer not available to serve monarch

parts.note: a dish no longer on the menu is off
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone unavailable to wait on the king or queen steps forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To volunteer something is to put it forward unasked, to proffer it.

clue.text: Friendly spirit

definitions.meaning: intimate, on close and easy terms
the attendant demon of a witch

explanation.surface: Two words describing a kindly ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Familiar means close and informal; a witch's familiar is the demon or spirit that attends her, often in animal form.

clue.text: Founder of state put on flag

parts.note: William Penn founded the American colony of Pennsylvania
taken as written, set after the founder's name

explanation.surface: The man who founded a state is placed on a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: Pennsylvania takes its name from William Penn, its seventeenth-century founder.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow pointed flag, as once carried on a knight's lance.

clue.text: Regimental type who patrols the Strand?

definitions.meaning: a soldier of the ..., a Household Cavalry regiment
strand meaning shore, someone keeping watch over bathers

explanation.surface: A soldier walking along London's famous street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a London street, but a strand is also a beach; the Life Guards are a British cavalry regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Life Guards regiment, or a swimmer employed to watch over bathers on a beach.

clue.text: Show sudden brilliance or talent, say

indicators.note: say signals a word heard rather than written, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: a flair is a natural aptitude or talent

explanation.surface: Advice to a performer: display sudden genius or natural gift.
explanation.definitionFit: To flare is to blaze up suddenly, burst briefly into bright light.

clue.text: It's a bloomer to back what comes last in Derby

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word Derby

explanation.surface: Backing the final runner in the Derby is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it is a flowering plant; the Derby is England's most famous flat horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Betony is a purple-flowered wild plant of the mint family, so something that blooms.

clue.text: American statesman, a Republican from the East

definitions.meaning: a man from an American state, the state of Georgia
a citizen of the eastern republic of Georgia

explanation.surface: A politician from the US belonging to the Republican party, from the eastern states.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'statesman' as state's man: someone from Georgia, a US state; and Georgia was also a Soviet republic, so a Georgian is a republican from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the US state of Georgia, or of the Caucasian former Soviet republic of the same name.

clue.text: Day on which nothing occurs in Northern town

parts.note: THURS is the abbreviation for Thursday
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A dull day in a town in the north when nothing happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Thurso is a town on the far north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Thurso is the most northerly town on the British mainland, in Caithness.

clue.text: Elevated upstart given acclaim

parts.note: read as 'up start', the start of the word up, a U
acclaimed means praised

explanation.surface: A social climber is promoted and showered with praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upstart' looks like a parvenu, but split it as 'up' plus 'start' to get the first letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Upraised means lifted up or raised high.

clue.text: Notice a change on the right in one facet of Conservatism

indicators.note: a change tells us to rearrange the letters of 'notice a'

explanation.surface: Observing a shift to the right within part of Tory thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the right' sounds political, but it only puts R at the front; 'Notice a change' looks like plain prose, yet 'change' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Political reaction is opposition to progress and a wish to restore the old order, one strand of conservative thinking.

clue.text: A narcotics bust? Not new in this country

indicators.note: bust as in broken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drugs raid in a Central American nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not new' removes N from A NARCOTICS, and 'bust' rearranges the remaining nine letters into the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa Rica is a republic in Central America.

clue.text: Main area in which chess player finds place for bishop, say

parts.note: one of the two sides in a chess game is Black

indicators.note: say signals a word heard, so the spelling changes

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A chess player looks for the square where his bishop should go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' wants to be the chess piece but is the churchman whose seat is a see; 'main' is old poetic for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea is a large inland sea between Europe and Asia, and 'the main' is an old word for the ocean.

clue.text: Northern area producing top-class wine to drink

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
red is a type of wine
ale is a drink, a beer

explanation.surface: A region in the north turning out first-class wine and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Airedale is the valley of the River Aire in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Airedale is the dale of the River Aire, a district in West Yorkshire.

clue.text: Witness present for trial

parts.note: to be present at somewhere is to be at it
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A witness attends for a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness, to vouch for the truth of something.

clue.text: English county returned deed conditionally held

indicators.note: returned says the county's short form is read backwards

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county

explanation.surface: A county in England sends back a contract held under conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns WORCS (Worcestershire) into SCROW.
explanation.definitionFit: An escrow is a bond or deed held by a third party until a condition is met.

clue.text: A famous master of fiction wrote so funnily

indicators.note: funnily signals the letters of 'wrote so' arranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: A well-known novelist who wrote comically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' suggests a writer, but Bertie Wooster is the young master served by Jeeves in P G Wodehouse's comic novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie Wooster, the young gentleman of Wodehouse's Jeeves stories, is perhaps the best-known master in fiction.

clue.text: Dance by the little comedian, say, is a work of art

parts.note: to trip is to dance lightly, as in 'trip the light fantastic'

indicators.note: say means the comedian's name is heard, with a different spelling

parts.note: Little Tich was a famous tiny music-hall comedian

explanation.surface: A tiny comic joins a dance, and the result is a piece of art.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Tich was a celebrated short Victorian music-hall comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A triptych is a painting or carving on three hinged panels, often an altarpiece.

clue.text: Track needed by fast railway

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A line required for an express train service.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or track, or the marks left by something passing.

clue.text: Monkey almost catches maiden in the tall grass

indicators.note: catches says one piece is held inside the other
almost says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a baboon is a large monkey
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A monkey nearly grabs a young woman in the long grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BABOON to BABOO, and 'catches' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is a giant woody grass that can grow very tall.

clue.text: Vessel with new cargo to carry

indicators.note: cargo says the letter is loaded inside the ship

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship

explanation.surface: A ship takes on a fresh load to transport.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring is to carry or convey something to a place.

clue.text: Work for Holmes or Watson, for instance

definitions.meaning: an investigation taken on by the detectives

explanation.surface: A detective's job, Watson for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is a matter for detectives to investigate, and also an instance or example of something.

clue.text: Female star one left out of column

indicators.note: out of says the letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Stella is a girl's name meaning star
L is the abbreviation for left; 'one' says only a single L goes

explanation.surface: An actress with one left out of the cast list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' takes one L from STELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stela is an upright stone slab or pillar, usually carved or inscribed.

clue.text: Ways in which a Liberal gets elected together with one Commie

indicators.note: in which says the following pieces sit inside the two ways

parts.note: ST is short for street, so two streets give ST ST
a candidate elected is in
I, the Roman numeral, is one

explanation.surface: A Liberal wins a seat by joining forces with a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts A, L, IN and I between the two STs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalinist is a hard-line communist, a follower of Stalin's methods.

clue.text: New Orleans antagonism for upper-class Londoner

indicators.note: new says the letters of Orleans are made into a new order

parts.note: anger is hostility or antagonism

explanation.surface: Hostility in a US city towards a posh visitor from London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' reads as the city, but 'New' rearranges ORLEANS. A Sloane Ranger is a stereotyped well-off young Londoner from around Sloane Square.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sloane Ranger is the stock posh, well-heeled young person of fashionable west London.
